sources.title: World of Change: Arctic Sea Ice - NASA Science
sources.excerpt: satellites have monitored sea ice growth and retreat... detected an overall decline

sources.title: Climate Change: Arctic sea ice summer minimum | NOAA Climate.gov
sources.excerpt: average minimum extent for each third of the satellite record has successively declined

sources.title: Arctic and Baltic sea ice | Indicators | European Environment Agency (EEA)
sources.excerpt: Arctic has lost an area of 71,000km 2 of sea ice per year

reasoning: Data from major scientific agencies including NASA, NOAA, and the European Environment Agency consistently demonstrate a statistically significant, long-term decline in Arctic sea ice extent since satellite monitoring began in the late 1970s. Both summer minimums and winter maximums show downward trends that go beyond short-term interannual variability.
